str: You haul anchor chains until the deck groans under your grip.
A sparring mast splinters after one clean, stubborn swing.
You shoulder cargo crates like cannonballs and keep moving.
spd: You sprint the rigging before the gulls can scatter.
A cannon drill turns into footwork practice across a rain-slick deck.
You slip between crashing waves and come back faster than you left.
def: You brace through a storm drill and refuse to give the deck an inch.
Your guard holds firm under a dozen wooden practice blades.
You learn where to plant your feet when the sea tries to take them.
will: You stare down the horizon until even the Log Pose settles.
A bad omen crosses the mast, and you keep your hand steady anyway.
You train through hunger, salt, and noise until your spirit hardens.
